newsitem.title: CANADA: Suncor to invest $2.2 bln in oil sands.
newsitem.headline: Suncor to invest $2.2 bln in oil sands.

text.p: Suncor Energy Inc said on Thursday it planned to invest C$2.2 billion to bring its bring oil sands production to 210,000 barrels a day by 2002.
It said the program, called Project Millenium, would twin the existing extraction and upgrading facilities and increase production to almost 250 percent of current levels.
It said the investment was in addition to the C$600 million of expansion projects under way at Suncor's oil sands facility in Fort McMurray, Alberta.
Suncor said the current initiatives were expected to bring production to 105,000 barrels a day by 1999. Suncor's oil sands business now produces about 85,000 barrels a day.

It said the first phase of Project Millennium was a C$190 million investment in the existing oil sands plant. That work, which would begin immediately, would gradually increase production to an estimated 130,000 barrels a day by 2001.
Suncor said the second phase would be led off by a C$90 million technical, environmental and socio-economic assessment to determine the best approach to the expansion.
The assessment will include comprehensive engineering work on the project and a public involvement process. Regulatory review is expected to begin this summer.
When the assessment is complete, Suncor's board will make a final decision on the configuration of the full expansion. Construction would start in 1999, subject to regulatory and board approval.
Suncor said that as its oil sands production rises, economies of scale and technological and reliability improvements were expected to send cash costs per barrel to record lows.

"When the 210,000 barrel-per-day target is reached in 2002, Suncor estimates its cash costs will be $10 to $11 per barrel compared with $15 per barrel today. At this cost, products from the company's Oil Sands business would be fully cost-competitive with most sources of crude in North America," Suncor said.

Suncor Chief Executive Rick George said in a statement that the C$2.2 billion investment was expected to generate a return on capital greater than 15 percent -- "more than double the average rate of return for the Canadian conventional oil and gas sector.

He added that "because Suncor's oil sands facility upgrades the bitumen from oil sands into light crude products, the increased production will have ready markets. We are confident that we will be able to find a home for this increased production.
